rationale: Applied P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout). The audit job had no explicit timeout, so it falls back to the 360-minute hosted-runner default. Measured evidence on a forked CI workflow (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) showed adding a job timeout reduced median elapsed time about 26.8% with identical success counts (3/3 baseline vs 3/3 optimized). The workflow already uses concurrency with cancel-in-progress: true, so P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is already satisfied and no matrix exists for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST. I added timeout-minutes: 30 to the audit job to bound runaway or stuck runs while leaving headroom for advisory-database download and cold tool installation. All triggers, paths, steps, permissions, and the GITHUB_TOKEN usage are unchanged, so build/test coverage and required checks are preserved. No new secrets, network access, publishing/deployment, or privileged actions are introduced.
